newsitem.title: UK: Diana Bosnia trip overshadowed by new man.
newsitem.headline: Diana Bosnia trip overshadowed by new man.

text.p: Princess Diana set off for Bosnia on Friday to crusade against landmines but her trip was in danger of being overshadowed by reports of a new man in her life.

Speculation about Diana's friendship with divorced, polo-playing film producer Dodi Fayed, 41, went into overdrive as tabloid newspapers said the princess had been seen entering his luxury London apartment for a dinner date.
The Daily Mail's front page headline read: "Diana - it's a real romance", while The Sun said: "Romantic meal in new love's London flat -- then farewell kiss before Bosnia".
Diana left London's Heathrow Airport in a private jet bound for Sarajevo. She was looking happy and relaxed in a blue denim shirt and tight blue slacks.
Her 15-year marriage to British royal heir Prince Charles ended in divorce last year.
Diana, 36, was due in Sarajevo for a "private visit" hosted by the Washington-based Landmine Survivors' Network to highlight the plight of victims of landmines.
The Foreign Office has given its clearance for the trip to go ahead.
After arriving in Sarajevo at midday, Diana was due to travel to the northeastern town of Tuzla, although her schedule was shrouded in secrecy for security reasons.

Diana was not expected to visit Serb-held areas of Bosnia, where anti-British feeling is running high following an operation by British special forces to arrest two Serbs wanted for war crimes which resulted in one of them being shot dead.
But even Moslem and Croat areas of Bosnia have been gripped by new tension, with Croat thugs driving Bosnian Moslems from their homes.
It is the second time Diana has visited a former war zone on her anti-mine campaign.
The first trip, to Angola in January, brought home to many around the world the terrible toll inflicted on civilians by the millions of anti-personnel mines left behind by war.
Whatever the merits of her campaign, news of Diana's "new best friend" had reached Bosnia even before her private jet touched down at Sarajevo's shell-battered airport on Friday afternoon.

Britain's royalty-obsessed tabloid newspapers have printed pictures of Diana on a boat enjoying a summer holiday in the Mediterranean with Dodi Fayed, the son of Mohammed Al-Fayed, the Egyptian tycoon who owns London's luxury department store Harrods.
"Princess Diana has embarked on her first serious romance since she and Charles divorced," the Daily Mail's royal correspondent Richard Kay said.
She was said to be so "relaxed" about the affair becoming public knowledge that she was "unconcerned" at the prospect of intimate photographs of the couple being published.
The new pictures, said to show the couple kissing, have been the subject of a bidding war among newspapers and magazines in Europe.

But the Daily Telegraph said the princess was known to be "extremely upset that her most ambitious mission in her campaign against landmines is likely to be upstaged by a set of pictures suggesting a new romance".
Mohammed Al-Fayed, who has also played host to Diana in the south of France this summer, welcomed the friendship between the princess and the playboy.
"I give them both my blessing. They are both adults. She is a lovely girl and he is my son and I love him very much," he told The Sun.
"They seem to enjoy each other's company a lot and it makes me happy to see them both so happy.
"I don't exactly know what their plans are for the future but as long as they both remain happy, that warms my heart."
Dodi Fayed was married for eight months, in 1986, to American model Suzanne Gregard.
He has also been romantically linked with a string of actresses, including Brooke Shields, Britt Ekland, Joanna Whalley and Frank Sinatra's daughter, Tina.
Fayed was executive producer of the British film "Chariots of Fire", which won an Oscar for best picture in 1982.
